rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the central tensor expansion, both factors have clean horizontal minus signs: (b_1-chi U_1) tensor (b_2-chi U_2). In the next line, the sign immediately before chi U has a thick horizontal bar crossed by an upright extending both above and below; it is a plus, resolving the original plus/minus uncertainty (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_tensor_signs.jpg). Between b_1 and b_2 in that same result, a cramped circular mark with crossing/overlapping strokes is visible; it is not represented by the original juxtaposition b_1b_2. A tensor symbol is the plausible reading, but the circle overlaps the adjoining subscript and b stem, so record it as \unsure{\otimes} (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_product_notation.jpg). The upper b double-prime_i equation clearly has a minus before chi U prime_i (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_second_change.jpg), whereas the preceding b prime_i equation has a plus (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_first_change.jpg). The separate composite tensor equation also uses minuses (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_composite_tensor.jpg), while the later uncancelled component formulas use plus signs (crops/84_scan132_L49_L1232_lower_plus.jpg). Preserve these written differences.
